html:
The Wasco and Wishram are Upper Chinookan peoples of the Columbia River gorge around The Dalles. The Wasco lived on the south bank, in Oregon, and the Wishram on the north bank, in Washington.

Their villages sat at the Long Narrows and Celilo Falls, the busiest fishing and trading place on the Columbia River. Peoples came from the coast and the interior to trade salmon, roots, shells, slaves and later horses; a trade jargon, related to the Chinook language, grew up there. The Lewis and Clark Expedition passed in 1805. Later the Oregon Trail ran through their land. In 1855 the Wasco went to the Warm Springs reservation with the Tenino, now the Confederated Tribes of Warm Springs, and most Wishram joined the Yakama. The Dalles Dam flooded Celilo Falls in 1957.
